<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Implement a series-parallel conversion circuit.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data.</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="cnt">Counter for the number of serial input data received.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt">Counter for the number of serial input data received.</reg>
        <reg id="din_tmp" width_description="[7:0]">Temporary storage for serial input data.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <![CDATA[
The module utilizes a 4-bit counter (cnt) to keep track of the number of serial input data bits received. When (cnt) reachs 8, (cnt) is reset to 0. Otherwise, (cnt) is reset to 0 if (rst_n) is negative, else (cnt) increases 1 every positive (clk) edge.
A `din_tmp` register is used to serialize the current `din_serial`. `din_tmp` is reset to 0 if (rst_n) is inactive. Otherwise, in every positive (clk), when `din_valid` is high and the (cnt) is less than or equal 7, `din_tmp` updates new `din_serial` by left shifting `din_tmp` and appending `din_serial` at the least significant bit of `din_tmp`.
When (cnt) reachs decimal digit 8 (not decimal digit 7), `dout_valid` is set to 1 and `dout_parallel` is set to `din_tmp` at the same positive (clk). Otherwise, `dout_valid` and `dout_parallel` is 0.
        ]]></implementation>
</module>

samples.xml_description:
Implement a simplified radix-2 divider on 8-bit signed or unsigned integers. The module accepts a dividend and a divisor as inputs and provides a 16-bit result containing both the quotient and the remainder. The design supports both signed and unsigned division operations. Clock signal used for synchronous operation. The reset signal to initialize or reset the module. 1-bit indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0). 8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division. 8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division. 1-bit indicates that a valid operation request is present. 1-bit indicates that the 16-bit output result has already been acknowledged. 1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready. res_valid must be constructed as combinational logic and not in any always block. So res_valid must not be declared as register. 16-bit the output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits. The parameter ADD represents the binary code for the addition operation in the ALU. The parameter SUB represents the binary code for the subtraction operation in the ALU. The parameter MUL represents the binary code for the multiplication operation in the ALU. The parameter DIV represents the binary code for the division operation in the ALU.

divisor_extend: 9-bit combinational logic. divisor_extend is set to concatenation of bit 1 and input divisor if the input sign and MSB of input divisor is high. Otherwise, divisor_extend is set to concatenation of bit 0 and input divisor.

NEG_DIVISOR: 9-bit sequencial logic.

all_sub_result 10-bit combinational logic.

sub_result: 9-bit combinational logic. sub_result is the first 9-bit of all_sub_result.

sub_remainer_reg_divisor: combinational logic operation. 10-bit all_sub_result is set to summation of REMAINER and NEG_DIVISOR.

REMAINER: 8-bit combinational logic. This is a subsection of 8-bit MSB of SR.

QUOTIENT: 8-bit combinational logic. This is a subsection of 8-bit LSB of SR.

CO: 1-bit combinational logic. CO is set to the MSB of all_sub_result.

mux_result: 9-bit combinational logic. If CO is high, mux_result is set to sub_result else set to REMAINER.

quotient_shift: 7-bit combinational logic. quotient_shift is set to 7 [7:1] bits of SR.

SR_final_update: sequencial logic operation. First, the 8-bit MSB of SR is set to 8-bit mux_result. Then bit [0:0] of SR is set to CO.

SR_shifting: sequencial logic operation. Concatenate SR from of first 7-bit of mux_result, 7-bit quotient_shift, 1-bit CO, and 1-bit zero.

dividend_abs: 8-bit combinational logic. If sign and the MSB of input dividend is high, dividend_abs is set to two's complement of the input dividend. Otherwise, dividend_abs is set to the original input dividend only.

final_remainer: 8-bit combinational logic. final_remainer is set to two's complement of REMAINER if the sign bit and MSB of register dividend is high. Otherwise, final_remainer is set to REMAINER.

final_quotient: 8-bit combinational logic. final_quotient is set to two's complement of QUOTIENT if sign and MSB of register dividend is high. Otherwise, final_quotient is set to QUOTIENT.

is_final_quotient_sign: 1-bit combinational logic. is_final_quotient_sign is result of the and logic of sign and the xor logic of MSB of dividend register and MSB of divisor register.

Operation Start:

  • When opn_valid is high, res_valid is low, and start_cnt is low, the module saves the inputs dividend and divisor in to 2 8-bit corresponding regisers.
  • Initializes the 16-bit shift register SR with the absolute value of the original input dividend (dividend_abs) shifted left by one bit.
  • 9-bit NEG_DIVISOR is set to divisor_extend, if the sign bit and MSB of divisor is high. Otherwise, sets 9-bit NEG_DIVISOR to two's complement of the divisor_extend.
  • Sets the 4-bit counter cnt to 1 and start_cnt to 1 to begin the division process.

Division Process(If start_cnt is high, the module performs the following steps):

  • If most significant bit of cnt is set (the counter cnt reaches 8), the division is complete:
    • cnt and start_cnt are cleared. Then, based on SR_final_update method, Updates the shift register SR with the final remainder and quotient.
  • Otherwise, the counter cnt is incremented, and the shift register SR is updated based on the subtraction result mux_result:
    • Based on sub_remainer_reg_divisor, compute the summation of NEG_DIVISOR and REMAINER.
    • Based on SR_shifting, updates SR.

Result Validity:

  • res_valid is managed based on the reset signal, the counter, and whether the result has been consumed, which is signaled by the input (res_ready).
  • res_valid should be update directly, without passing middle register value.
  • res_valid is set to zero if rst is high.
  • Otherwise, if cnt reaches 8, res_ready is set to 1.
  • Otherwise, if res_valid and res_ready is all high, res_valid is set to 0. Otherwise, res_valid is set to res_valid.

Result operation:

  • The output result is constructed as combinational logic and is set to concatenation of final_remainer and final_quotient. Notice that, because of combinational operation, the result must not be calculated in any always block.

Implement a data width conversion circuit that converts 8-bit data input to 16-bit data output. Clock signal used for synchronous operation. Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive. Input signal indicating the validity of the input data. 8-bit input data to be converted. Output signal indicating the validity of the output data. 16-bit output data resulting from the width conversion. Input data width. Output data width. Register to store the first valid input data. Flag signal to indicate the arrival of the first valid input data.

Reset the data_out register to 0 when the reset signal is active (negedge rst_n).

When the input data is valid (valid_in) and the flag signal is active, concatenate the contents of the data_lock register and the data_in register to update the data_out register.

Set the flag signal to 1 when the first valid input data is received.

Reset the flag signal to 0 when the second valid input data is received.

<module id="traffic_light">
    <description>Implement a traffic light with three small red, yellow and green indicators and a pedestrian button. Under normal circumstances, the motor vehicle lane indicator light according to 60 clock cycles of green, 5 clock cycles of yellow, 10 clock cycles of red. When the pedestrian button is pressed, if the remaining green time is greater than 10 clocks, it is shortened to 10 clocks, and if it is less than 10 clocks, it remains unchanged. The lane light and the sidewalk light should be paired, when the lane light is green or yellow, the sidewalk light is red; When the lane light is red, the sidewalk light is green, and for the sake of simplicity, only the lane light is considered.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="pass_request">Request signal for allowing vehicles to pass.</input>
        <output id="clock" width_description="[7:0]">An 8-bit output representing the count value of the internal counter.</output>
        <output id="red">Red light output.</output>
        <output id="yellow">Yellow light output.</output>
        <output id="green">Green light output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="idle">0. IDLE state</parameter>
        <parameter id="s1_red">1. Red light state</parameter>
        <parameter id="s2_yellow">2. Yellow light state</parameter>
        <parameter id="s3_green">3. Green light state</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="cnt">Internal counter. If rst_n is deactive, cnt is 10 decimal. Otherwise, if pass_request is active and green is active and cnt is greater than 10, cnt is 10 decimal. Otherwise, if green is deactive and p_green is active, cnt is 60 decimal. Otherwise, if yellow is deactive and p_yellow is active, cnt is 5 decimal. Otherwise, if red is deactive and p_red is active, cnt is 10 decimal. Otherwise, cnt is decremented by 1 on every positive edge of the clock.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="state">If rst_n is deactive, state is idle. Otherwise, in case state is idle, state is s1_red. In case state is s1_red, if cnt counts to 3 decimal, state is s3_green, else state is s1_red. In case state is s2_yellow, if cnt counts to 3 decimal, state is s1_red, else state is s2_yellow. In case state is s3_green, if cnt counts to 3 decimal, state is s2_yellow, else state is s3_green.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="p_red">If rst_n is deactive, p_red is reset to 0. Otherwise, red is set to 1 if state is s1_red, yellow is set to 1 if state is s2_yellow, and green is set to 1 if state is s3_green.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="p_green">If rst_n is deactive, p_green is reset to 0. Otherwise, red is set to 1 if state is s1_red, yellow is set to 1 if state is s2_yellow, and green is set to 1 if state is s3_green.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="p_yellow">If rst_n is deactive, p_yellow is reset to 0. Otherwise, red is set to 1 if state is s1_red, yellow is set to 1 if state is s2_yellow, and green is set to 1 if state is s3_green.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="red">If rst_n is deactive, red is reset to 0. Otherwise, red is set to p_red.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="green">If rst_n is deactive, green is reset to 0. Otherwise, green is set to p_green.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="yellow">If rst_n is deactive, yellow is reset to 0. Otherwise, yellow is set to p_yellow.</sequential_logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <description>
            The first always block is responsible for the state transition logic, based on description of sequential logic state. Notice that the the state only change when the counter cnt reaches 3 decimal.
            The second always block is responsible for internal counter cnt logic.
            The assign statement assigns the value of the internal counter (cnt) to the output clock.
            The final always block handles the output signals. It assigns the previous values (p_red, p_yellow, p_green) to the output signals (red, yellow, green) on the positive edge of the clock or negative edge of the reset signal.
            Notice to handle sequencial logic for state and cnt correctly.
        </description>
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_16bit">
    <description>Implement an unsigned 16-bit multiplier with shift and accumulate operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Chip clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="start">Chip enable signal to initiate the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="ain" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand (a) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <input id="bin" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier (b) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <output id="yout" width_description="[31:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 32 bits.</output>
        <output id="done">Chip output flag signal. Defined as 1 indicates the completion of the multiplication operation.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="i">Shift count register. Incremented when start is active and i is less than 17. Reset to 0 when start is inactive.</parameter>
        <parameter id="done_r">Multiplication completion flag. Set to 1 when i is equal to 16. Reset to 0 when i is equal to 17.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <description>Data bit control.</description>
        <reg id="i" type="sequential_logic">
            <description>Shift count register. Incremented when start is active and i is less than 17. Reset to 0 when start is inactive.</description>
            <initial_value>0</initial_value>
            <always>
                <description>On every positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the shift count register (i) is updated.</description>
                <trigger id="clk" posedge="true" negedge="true">
                    <description>At positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n).</description>
                    <if condition="!rst_n">
                        <description>Reset condition. The shift count register (i) is set to 0.</description>
                        <assignment id="i" value="0" />
                    </if>
                    <else>
                        <description>Start condition. The shift count register (i) is updated.</description>
                        <if condition="start && i < 17">
                            <description>The shift count register (i) is incremented by 1.</description>
                            <assignment id="i" value="i + 1" />
                        </if>
                        <else>
                            <description>The shift count register (i) is reset to 0.</description>
                            <assignment id="i" value="0" />
                        </else>
                    </else>
                </trigger>
            </reg>
        </always>
        <description>Multiplication completion flag generation.</description>
        <reg id="done_r" type="sequential_logic">
            <description>Multiplication completion flag. Set to 1 when i is equal to 16. Reset to 0 when i is equal to 17.</description>
            <initial_value>0</initial_value>
            <always>
                <description>On every positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the multiplication completion flag (done_r) is updated.</description>
                <trigger id="clk" posedge="true" negedge="true">
                    <description>At positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n).</description>
                    <if condition="!rst_n">
                        <description>Reset condition. The multiplication completion flag (done_r) is set to 0.</description>
                        <assignment id="done_r" value="0" />
                    </if>
                    <else>
                        <description>Start condition. The multiplication completion flag (done_r) is updated.</description>
                        <if condition="i == 16">
                            <description>The multiplication completion flag (done_r) is set to 1.</description>
                            <assignment id="done_r" value="1" />
                        </if>
                        <else>
                            <description>The multiplication completion flag (done_r) is reset to 0.</description>
                            <if condition="i == 17">
                                <assignment id="done_r" value="0" />
                            </if>
                        </else>
                    </else>
                </trigger>
            </reg>
        </always>
        <description>Shift and accumulate operation.</description>
        <reg id="yout_r" type="sequential_logic">
            <description>Product register. Updated based on the shift count register (i).</description>
            <initial_value>0</initial_value>
            <always>
                <description>On every positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the module performs the shift and accumulate operation.</description>
                <trigger id="clk" posedge="true" negedge="true">
                    <description>At positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n).</description>
                    <if condition="!rst_n">
                        <description>Reset condition. The multiplicand register (areg), multiplier register (breg), and product register (yout_r) are reset to 0.</description>
                        <assignment id="yout_r" value="0" />
                    </if>
                    <else>
                        <description>Start condition. The module starts the multiplication operation.</description>
                        <if condition="start">
                            <description>The multiplicand (ain) and multiplier (bin) are stored in the respective registers (areg and breg).</description>
                            <if condition="i == 0">
                                <assignment id="areg" value="ain" />
                                <assignment id="breg" value="bin" />
                            </if>
                            <else>
                                <description>For shift counts greater than 0 and less than 17, if the bit at position i-1 in the multiplicand register (areg) is high, the product register (yout_r) accumulates the shifted value of the multiplier register (breg) by shifting it left by i-1 positions and appending zeros at the least significant bit positions.</description>
                                <if condition="areg[i-1] && i < 17">
                                    <assignment id="yout_r" value="yout_r + (breg << (i-1))" />
                                </if>
                            </else>
                        </if>
                    </else>
                </trigger>
            </reg>
        </always>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Reset the registers and perform shift and accumulate operations to compute the product.</implementation>
    <output>
        <description>The product output (yout) is assigned the value of the product register (yout_r).</description>
        <assignment id="yout" value="yout_r" />
        <description>The done output is assigned the value of the done register (done_r).</description>
        <assignment id="done" value="done_r" />
    </output>
</module>

    <description>Implement an unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="MUL_WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="MUL_OUT_WIDTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_en_out_reg">
            <description>mul_en_out_reg is a 3-bit register that stores the input enable signal mul_en_in. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The value of mul_en_out_reg is concatenated by its previous two bits and the bit value of mul_en_in.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>mul_en_out_reg <= {mul_en_out_reg[1:0], mul_en_in};</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="mul_en_out">
            <description>mul_en_out is a combinational logic that outputs the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg.</description>
            <output>mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg[2];</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_a_reg">
            <description>mul_a_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input signal mul_a. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The register is only updated when the input enable signal is active.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>if (mul_en_in) mul_a_reg <= mul_a;</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_b_reg">
            <description>mul_b_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input signal mul_b. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The register is only updated when the input enable signal is active.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>if (mul_en_in) mul_b_reg <= mul_b;</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp">
            <description>temp is a 8-bit wire array that stores the partial products. Each wire corresponds to a partial product generated by the bitwise AND operation between the corresponding bit of mul_a_reg and the entire mul_b_reg.</description>
            <output>temp[0] = mul_a_reg[0] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[1] = mul_a_reg[1] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[2] = mul_a_reg[2] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[3] = mul_a_reg[3] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[4] = mul_a_reg[4] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[5] = mul_a_reg[5] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[6] = mul_a_reg[6] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
            <output>temp[7] = mul_a_reg[7] ? mul_b_reg : 0;</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum">
            <description>sum is a 16-bit wire array that stores the partial sums. Each wire corresponds to a partial sum generated by the addition of the corresponding partial products. The first partial sum is the first partial product, and the remaining partial sums are generated by the addition of the previous partial sum and the next partial product.</description>
            <output>sum[0] = temp[0];</output>
            <output>sum[1] = temp[1];</output>
            <output>sum[2] = temp[2] + temp[3];</output>
            <output>sum[3] = temp[3] + temp[4];</output>
            <output>sum[4] = temp[4] + temp[5];</output>
            <output>sum[5] = temp[5] + temp[6];</output>
            <output>sum[6] = temp[6] + temp[7];</output>
            <output>sum[7] = temp[7];</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_out_reg">
            <description>mul_out_reg is a 16-bit register that stores the final product. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal. The register is updated by adding all the partial sums.</description>
            <update_event>posedge clk</update_event>
            <update_action>mul_out_reg <= sum[0] + sum[1] + sum[2] + sum[3] + sum[4] + sum[5] + sum[6] + sum[7];</update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="mul_out">
            <description>mul_out is a combinational logic that outputs the final product. If the output enable signal is active, the output is the value in mul_out_reg. Otherwise, the output is 0.</description>
            <output>mul_out = mul_en_out ? mul_out_reg : 0;</output>
        </combinational_logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implement an unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing. It utilizes a clock signal (clk), an active-low reset signal (rst_n), an input enable signal (mul_en_in), and provides an output enable signal (mul_en_out) and the product output (mul_out) of size 16 bits.</implementation>

<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Implement a parallel to serial converter with MSB to LSB order.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal for serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial data output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="s0">State 0.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s1">State 1.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s2">State 2.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s3">State 3.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <description>
            <item>Output:</item>
            <item>Output is the most significant bit of data.</item>
        </description>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <description>
            <item>When the counter is 3, the last bit of the parallel input is output.</item>
            <item>The counter is reset to 0, and the valid signal is set to 1.</item>
            <item>Otherwise, the counter is incremented by 1, and the valid signal is set to 0.</item>
            <item>The data register is shifted left by 1.</item>
            <item>When the counter is 3, the data register is updated with the parallel input.</item>
        </description>
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>Implement a 16-bit divider module, the dividend is 16-bit and the divider is 8-bit in combinational logic. Extract the higher bits of the dividend, matching the bit width of the divisor. Compare these bits with the divisor: if the dividend bits are greater, set the quotient to 1, otherwise set it to 0, and use the difference as the remainder. Concatenate the remainder with the highest remaining 1-bit of the dividend, and repeat the process until all dividend bits are processed.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit dividend.</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit divisor.</input>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit quotient.</output>
        <output id="odd" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit remainder.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="ADD=6'b100000">ADD</parameter>
        <parameter id="SUB=6'b100010">SUB</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRA">SRA</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRL">SRL</parameter>
    </parameter_description>

        <line>always @(A or B)</line>
        <line>if (A > B)</line>
        <line>result = 1'b1;</line>
        <line>else</line>
        <line>result = 1'b0;</line>
        <line>odd = A - B;</line>
    </logic_description>

samples.xml_description:
Implement an 8-bit multiplier based on shifting and adding operations. First 8-bit input operand (multiplicand). Second 8-bit input operand (multiplier). 16-bit output representing the product of A and B. Parameter N represents the number of bits for inputs A and B. Loop index for iterating through the bits of input B. Shifted version of input A, initialized with A and updated in the loop. Temporary variable to hold the intermediate product, initialized with 0 and updated in the loop. Variable to store the carry from the addition, initialized with 0 and updated in the loop.

Initialize the loop index i to 0 and set the temporary product and carry to 0.

Iterate through each bit of input B using a for loop:

  1. Check if the current bit of B is set (1).
  2. If it is, add the shifted version of A (stored in shifted_A) to the temporary product (product_temp) and store the result.
  3. Update the carry with the result of the addition.
  4. Shift the multiplicand A left by one bit to prepare for the next iteration.

After the loop completes, assign the final product to the output product.

<module id="freq_div">
    <description>Design a frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency of 100MHz into 50MHz, 10MHz, and 1MHz signals.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
        <output id="CLK_50">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 2.</output>
        <output id="CLK_10">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 10.</output>
        <output id="CLK_1">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 100.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="div_50">Parameter for dividing the clock frequency by 2.</parameter>
        <parameter id="div_10">Parameter for dividing the clock frequency by 10.</parameter>
        <parameter id="div_1">Parameter for dividing the clock frequency by 100.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="div_50">
            <description>Divide the input clock frequency by 2.</description>
            <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
            <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
            <output id="CLK_50">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 2.</output>
            <implementation>
                <assign id="CLK_50">The output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 2.</assign>
                <always id="always_div_50">
                    <description>On every positive edge of CLK_in or RST, if RST is active, CLK_50 is set to 0. Otherwise, CLK_50 is toggled by inverting its current value.</description>
                    <trigger>posedge CLK_in or posedge RST</trigger>
                    <if id="if_div_50">
                        <condition>RST</condition>
                        <then>
                            <assign id="CLK_50=0">Set CLK_50 to 0.</assign>
                        </then>
                        <else>
                            <assign id="CLK_50=~CLK_50">Invert the current value of CLK_50.</assign>
                        </else>
                    </if>
                </always>
            </implementation>
        </sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="div_10">
            <description>Divide the input clock frequency by 10.</description>
            <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
            <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
            <output id="CLK_10">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 10.</output>
            <implementation>
                <assign id="CLK_10">The output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 10.</assign>
                <always id="always_div_10">
                    <description>On every positive edge of CLK_in or RST, if RST is active, CLK_10 is set to 0, and the counter cnt_10 is reset to 0. If the counter cnt_10 reaches a value of 9, CLK_10 is toggled by inverting its current value, and the counter cnt_10 is reset to 0. Otherwise, the counter cnt_10 is incremented by 1.</description>
                    <trigger>posedge CLK_in or posedge RST</trigger>
                    <if id="if_div_10">
                        <condition>RST</condition>
                        <then>
                            <assign id="CLK_10=0">Set CLK_10 to 0.</assign>
                            <assign id="cnt_10=0">Reset the counter cnt_10 to 0.</assign>
                        </then>
                        <else>
                            <if id="if_cnt_10">
                                <condition>cnt_10==9</condition>
                                <then>
                                    <assign id="CLK_10=~CLK_10">Invert the current value of CLK_10.</assign>
                                    <assign id="cnt_10=0">Reset the counter cnt_10 to 0.</assign>
                                </then>
                                <else>
                                    <assign id="cnt_10=cnt_10+1">Increment the counter cnt_10 by 1.</assign>
                                </else>
                            </if>
                        </else>
                    </if>
                </always>
            </implementation>
        </sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="div_1">
            <description>Divide the input clock frequency by 100.</description>
            <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
            <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
            <output id="CLK_1">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 100.</output>
            <implementation>
                <assign id="CLK_1">The output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 100.</assign>
                <always id="always_div_1">
                    <description>On every positive edge of CLK_in or RST, if RST is active, CLK_1 is set to 0, and the counter cnt_100 is reset to 0. samples.xml_description:
<module id="alu">
    <description>Implement an ALU for a 32-bit MIPS-ISA CPU.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">A 32-bit input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">A 32-bit input operand.</input>
        <input id="aluc" width_description="[5:0]">A 6-bit control signal for selecting the operation to be performed.</input>
        <output id="r" width_description="[31:0]">A 32-bit output representing the result of the operation.</output>
        <output id="zero">A 1-bit output indicating whether the result is zero.</output>
        <output id="carry">A 1-bit output indicating whether a carry occurred during the operation.</output>
        <output id="negative">A 1-bit output indicating whether the result is negative.</output>
        <output id="overflow">A 1-bit output indicating whether an overflow occurred during the operation.</output>
        <output id="flag">A 1-bit output representing a general flag, which is set based on specific operations (SLT and SLTU).</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="ADD">6'b100000</parameter>
        <parameter id="ADDU">6'b100001</parameter>
        <parameter id="SUB">6'b100010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SUBU">6'b100011</parameter>
        <parameter id="AND">6'b100100</parameter>
        <parameter id="OR">6'b100101</parameter>
        <parameter id="XOR">6'b100110</parameter>
        <parameter id="NOR">6'b100111</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLT">6'b101010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLTU">6'b101011</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLL">6'b000000</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRL">6'b000010</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRA">6'b000011</parameter>
        <parameter id="SLLV">6'b000100</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRLV">6'b000110</parameter>
        <parameter id="SRAV">6'b000111</parameter>
        <parameter id="LUI">6'b001111</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="res">
            <description>combinational logic. The output res is assigned to the lower 32 bits of the register res[32:0].</description>
            <assign id="res[31:0]" value="r"/>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="zero">
            <description>combinational logic. zero flag is active if res is all 0.</description>
            <assign id="zero" value="~(|res)"/>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="carry">
            <description>combinational logic. carry is equalled to the MSB of the output r in cases ADD, ADDU, SUB, and SUBU ALU opcodes. otherwise, carry is 0.</description>
            <assign id="carry" value="((aluc == `ADD) | (aluc == `ADDU) | (aluc == `SUB) | (aluc == `SUBU)) ? r[31] : 1'b0;"/>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="overflow">
            <description>combinational logic. in case ADD ALU opcode, overflow is active if (MSB of a is deactive, MSB of b is deactive, and MSB of r is active) or (MSB of a is active, MSB of b is active, and MSB of r is deactive). in case SUB ALU opcode, overflow is active if (MSB of a is active, MSB of b is deactive, and MSB of r is deactive) or (MSB of a is deactive, MSB of b is deactive, and MSB of r is active). otherwise, overflow is 0.</description>
            <assign id="overflow" value="((aluc == `ADD) & ((~a[31]) & (~b[31]) & r[31]) | ((a[31]) & (b[31]) & (~r[31]))) | ((aluc == `SUB) & ((a[31]) & (~b[31]) & (~r[31])) | ((~a[31]) & (b[31]) & r[31]));"/>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="r">
            <description>combinational logic. r is assigned to the lower 32 bits of the register res[32:0].</description>
            <assign id="r" value="res[31:0]"/>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="negative">
            <description>combinational logic. negative is set to the MSB of the output r.</description>
            <assign id="negative" value="r[31]"/>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="flag">
            <description>combinational logic. in case of SLT opcode, flag is active if 32-bit signed a is less than 32-bit signed b. in case of SLTU opcode, flag is active if 32-bit unsigned a is less than 32-bit unsigned b. otherwise, flag is 0.</description>
            <assign id="flag" value="((aluc == `SLT) & ($signed(a) < $signed(b))) | ((aluc == `SLTU) & (a < b));"/>
        </combinational_logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implement the ALU logic using combinational logic. Use the parameter descriptions to determine the logic for each operation.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>Implement a 4-bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">Multiplicand.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">Multiplier.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">Product.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="size">4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="partial_products" width_description="[2*size-1:0]">Array to store partial products.</reg>
        <reg id="registers" width_description="[2*size-1:0]">Array to store intermediate sum values.</reg>
        <reg id="product" width_description="[2*size-1:0]">Product accumulator.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <!-- Multiplication operation -->
        <for>
            <from>0</from>
            <to>size-1</to>
            <do>
                <if>
                    <true>partial_products[i] = mul_a << i;</true>
                    <false>partial_products[i] = 'd0;</false>
                </if>
            </do>
        </for>
        <!-- Add of partial products -->
        <for>
            <from>0</from>
            <to>size/2-1</to>
            <do>
                <if>
                    <true>registers[i] <= partial_products[2*i] + partial_products[2*i+1];</true>
                    <false>registers[i] <= 'd0;</false>
                </if>
            </do>
        </for>
        <!-- Final product calculation -->
        <always>
            <trigger>
                <true>clk posedge or rst_n negedge</true>
            </trigger>
            <do>
                <if>
                    <true>rst_n == 0, product <= 0;</true>
                    <false>product <= registers;</false>
                </if>
            </do>
        </always>
        <assign>
            <lhs>mul_out</lhs>
            <rhs>product</rhs>
        </assign>
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>Implement an asynchronous FIFO, FIFO bit width and depth can be configured(parameter DEPTH = 16, parameter WIDTH = 8). The asynchronous FIFO structure is divided into several parts. The first part is dual-port RAM, which is used for data storage. Instantiate dual-port RAM as a submodule, The RAM ports are input wclk, input wenc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] waddr, input [WIDTH-1:0] wdata, input rclk, input renc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] raddr, output reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata. The second part is the data write controller. The third part is the data read controller. The fourth part is the read pointer synchronizer. The read pointer is collected using the two-stage trigger of the write clock and output to the data write controller. The fifth part is the write pointer synchronizer, which uses the two-stage trigger of the read clock to collect the write pointer and output it to the data read controller.
The method of empty and full judgment is to generate empty and full signals by comparing the Gray code. Use 4-bit Gray code as a read/write pointer for a FIFO with depth 8. The gray code is converted to a four-digit binary number, using the lower three digits of the binary number as the address to access RAM. When the read and write Pointers are equal, the FIFO is null.
When the write pointer has one more cycle RAM than the read pointer, the highest and second-highest bits of the read and write pointer are opposite, the remaining bits are the same, and the FIFO is full.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="rstn">Reset signal used for synchronous reset operations.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8. Bit width of data input and output.</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">16. Depth of FIFO.</parameter>
        <parameter id="ADDR_WIDTH">4. Address width of FIFO.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential id="raddr_bin">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] raddr_bin; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. if rrstn is deactive, raddr_bin is all zero. otherwise, raddr_bin is incremented by 1 if rempty is deactive and rinc is active.</sequential>
        <combinational id="raddr_gray">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] raddr_gray; combinational logic. raddr_gray is XOR operation between raddr_bin and shift-left-1 operation of raddr_bin.</combinational>
        <sequential id="rptr">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. if rrstn is deactive, rptr is all zero. otherwise, rptr is set to raddr_gray.</sequential>
        <sequential id="rptr_buff">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr_buff; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. if wrstn is deactive, rptr_buff is all zero. otherwise, rptr_buff is set to rptr.</sequential>
        <sequential id="rptr_syn">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr_syn; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. if wrstn is deactive, rptr_syn is all zero. otherwise, rptr_syn is set to rptr_buff.</sequential>
        <combinational id="ren">reg ren; combinational logic. internal read enable logic. ren is active if rinc is active and rempty is deactive.</combinational>
        <sequential id="waddr_bin">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] waddr_bin; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. if wrstn is deactive, waddr_bin is all zero. otherwise, waddr_bin is incremented by 1 if wfull is deactive and winc is active.</sequential>
        <combinational id="waddr_gray">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] waddr_gray; combinational logic. waddr_gray is XOR operation between waddr_bin and shift-left-1 operation of waddr_bin.</combinational>
        <sequential id="wptr">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. if wrstn is deactive, wptr is all zero. otherwise, wptr is set to waddr_gray.</sequential>
        <combinational id="wfull">reg wfull; combinational logic. wfull is active if wptr is equaled to bitwise negation of 2 most significant bits of rptr_syn concatenated with remaining bits of rptr_syn.</combinational>
        <sequential id="wptr_buff">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_buff; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. if rrstn is deactive, wptr_buff is all zero. otherwise, wptr_buff is set to wptr.</sequential>
        <sequential id="wptr_syn">reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_syn; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. if rrstn is deactive, wptr_syn is all zero. otherwise, wptr_syn is set to wptr_buff.</sequential>
        <combinational id="wen">reg wen; combinational logic. internal write enable logic. wen is active if winc is active and wfull is deactive.</combinational>
        <combinational id="rempty">reg rempty; combinational logic. rempty is active if rptr is equaled to wptr_syn.</combinational>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        <description>
            The module implements an asynchronous FIFO using a dual-port RAM module and additional logic for managing read and write pointers.
            Dual-port RAM:
            The module instantiates a dual-port RAM module named "dual_port_RAM" with configurable depth and width.  
            The RAM module has separate clock inputs for write (wclk) and read (rclk) operations.
            The RAM module has separate address inputs for write (waddr) and read (raddr) operations.
            The RAM module has a write enable input (wenc) and a write data input (wdata).
            The RAM module has a read enable input (renc) and a read data output (rdata).
            The RAM module stores data in a two-dimensional array, RAM_MEM, with a size of DEPTH by WIDTH.
            The following logics from the top module "asyn_fifo" are used to instantiates the "dual_port_RAM": wclk, wen, waddr, wdata, rclk, ren, raddr, rdata:
            - wclk to wclk of "asyn_fifo".
            - wen to wen of "asyn_fifo".
            - waddr to waddr of "asyn_fifo".
            - wdata to wdata of "asyn_fifo".
            - rclk to rclk of "asyn_fifo".
            - ren to ren of "asyn_fifo".
            - raddr to raddr of "asyn_fifo".
            - rdata to rdata of "asyn_fifo".
            Write and Read Pointers:
            The module includes logic to manage write and read pointers for asynchronous operation.
            The write and read pointers are represented by binary registers, waddr_bin and raddr_bin, respectively.
            The waddr_bin and raddr_bin pointers are incremented based on the write and read increment signals (winc and rinc), respectively.
            The write pointer waddr_bin is incremented on the positive edge of the write clock (posedge wclk) and reset to 0 on write reset (~wrstn).
            The read pointer raddr_bin is incremented on the positive edge of the read clock (posedge rclk) and reset to 0 on read reset (~rrstn).
            Gray Code Conversion:
            The write and read pointers are converted to Gray code using XOR operations with right-shifted values.
            The converted write and read pointers are stored in registers wptr and rptr, respectively.
            The Gray code conversion reduces glitches and ensures proper synchronization of the write and read pointers.
            Pointer Buffers:
            The module includes buffer registers (wptr_buff and rptr_buff) to hold the previous values of the write and read pointers.
            The buffer registers are updated on the positive edge of the respective clocks and reset to 0 on the respective resets (~wrstn and ~rrstn).

The waveform cycles between 0 and 31, which is incremented or decremented by 1. Clock signal used for synchronous operation. Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive. 5-bit output waveform signal representing the generated waveform. FSM state variable used for controlling the waveform generation. Next state variable for controlling the waveform generation. Next wave variable for storing the updated waveform value.

State and Waveform Generation:

The module includes a register, state, used to control the state of the waveform generation.

The module also includes a register, wave, with a width of 5 bits, which represents the generated waveform.

The state and wave registers are updated in the always block, triggered on the positive edge of the clock signal (posedge clk) or the negative edge of the reset signal (negedge rst_n).

On reset, indicated by ~rst_n, the state register is cleared to 0, and the wave register is set to cleared to 0.

The state is transitioned between 0 and 1 based on the value of the wave register. In state 0, the waveform is incremented by 1 if the waveform differs 31 (wave != 31). Otherwise, if the waveform reaches 31 (wave == 31), the state is transitioned to 1. In state 1, the waveform is decremented by 1 if the waveform differs 0 (wave != 0). Otherwise, if the waveform reaches 0 (wave == 0), the state is transitioned back to 0.

The waveform generation continues to cycle between 0 and 31 based on the state transitions.

<module id="synchronizer">
    <description>Implement a multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer. The input data will remain constant during the period when data_en is high, and data_en is high for at least 3 clk_b clock cycles. When the value of data_en is high, data can be synchronized. The data change frequency of data_in is very low. The change interval between two adjacent data is at least 10 clk_b clock cycles. clk_a is responsible for data_in and data_en. clk_b is responsible for the 2 D flip-flops.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a">Clock signal A.</input>
        <input id="clk_b">Clock signal B.</input>
        <input id="arstn">Active-low reset signal A.</input>
        <input id="brstn">Active-low reset signal B.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal.</input>
        <input id="data_en">Input enable signal.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="data_reg">Data register to store input data.</parameter>
        <parameter id="en_data_reg">Enable data register to store input enable signal.</parameter>
        <parameter id="en_clap_one">Enable control register 1 to control data.</parameter>
        <parameter id="en_clap_two">Enable control register 2 to control data.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="data_reg">Data register is updated on the positive edge of clk_a or the negative edge of arstn. If arstn is low, data_reg is reset to 0. Otherwise, data_reg is updated with data_in.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="en_data_reg">Enable data register is updated on the positive edge of clk_a or the negative edge of arstn. If arstn is low, en_data_reg is reset to 0. Otherwise, en_data_reg is updated with data_en.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="en_clap_one">Enable control register 1 is updated on the positive edge of clk_b or the negative edge of brstn. If brstn is low, en_clap_one is reset to 0. Otherwise, en_clap_one is updated with en_data_reg.</sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="en_clap_two">Enable control register 2 is updated on the positive edge of clk_b or the negative edge of brstn. If brstn is low, en_clap_two is reset to 0. Otherwise, en_clap_two is updated with en_clap_one.</sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="dataout">Output data is updated on the positive edge of clk_b or the negative edge of brstn. If brstn is low, dataout is reset to 0. Otherwise, if en_clap_two is high, dataout is updated with data_reg. If en_clap_two is low, dataout retains its previous value.</combinational_logic>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation></implementation>
</module>
